author: Gould, 1836
status: 텃새 수백 마리 · 나그네새 수십 마리
summary: 울릉도에 흔한 텃새로, 주택지에서 멀지 않은 곳에 살며 큰키나무 구멍에 깃든다. 한배에 알을 5~7개 낳는다. 쌀, 조, 피 같은 곡식을 즐겨 먹고 여름에는 곤충도 잡아먹는다. 울릉도와 제주도, 남부 연안에서 살며, 국외로는 일본, 중국, 시베리아에 분포한다.

points.en: whitish grey-brown band on the hindcrown in winter (male)

sexes.male: 윗면은 진한 적갈색에 검은 세로줄무늬가 있고 아랫면은 흰빛에 가까운 황갈색이며 뺨이 희다. 겨울깃에는 뒷머리에 흰빛이 도는 회갈색 띠가 있다.

art.subject: Russet Sparrow (Passer cinnamomeus), adult male in breeding plumage (spring and summer): crown, nape, mantle and back rich chestnut, the mantle streaked black; a narrow black line from the bill to the eye; cheeks and ear coverts plain whitish, without any dark spot; a small black bib on the chin and upper throat; underparts whitish-buff, washed pale grey on the breast and flanks; wing coverts chestnut with a bold white wing bar, flight feathers dark brown with buff edges; tail brown; bill black; dark eye; pinkish-brown legs.
art.pose: perched at the entrance of a tree cavity, side view
art.scene: Tall broadleaf trees with nest holes near farmland on Ulleungdo island, Korea; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding, side view perched: rich chestnut crown, nape and back with black streaks on the mantle, plain whitish cheeks, small black bib, whitish-buff underparts, white wing bar, black bill
adult male winter, side view perched: same pattern, but the chestnut crown and nape partly veiled by pale greyish-brown feather tips, forming a whitish grey-brown band on the hindcrown
adult female, side view perched: brown upperparts streaked darker, broad greyish-white supercilium behind the eye, dark brown eye-stripe, pale buff underparts, pale horn bill
art.build: Small sparrow, 13cm, slightly smaller and slimmer than Eurasian Tree Sparrow (Passer montanus), with a rounded head and short neck. Bill short, stout and conical, shorter than the head. Legs short, pinkish-brown. Tail medium length, slightly notched. Perches on branches near tree holes and hops on the ground. A bold white wing bar shows on the folded wing.
avoid: Do not paint a black spot on the white cheek — that is Eurasian Tree Sparrow (Passer montanus); the Russet Sparrow's cheek is plain.
Do not paint a large black bib spreading onto the breast; the male's bib is small and limited to the chin and upper throat.
Do not paint a dull brown crown with a grey centre; the male's crown, nape and back are uniformly chestnut.
Do not give the female a bib or cheek spot; she is plain brown with a pale supercilium.
